issues.description: Identifier naming mismatch in solution_repository/aufgabe08.sql: the FROM clause references table Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde (line 2) while the WHERE clause references Radweg_zu_Gemeinde (line 3). The problem statement (Aufgabe 08) asks for a count of Radwege adjacent to Gemeinden with PLZ > 96400. This inconsistency will cause an SQL error (unknown table reference) or prevent the query from returning the intended result, blocking students from executing the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same table name in FROM and WHERE. Replace Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde with Radweg_zu_Gemeinde in the FROM clause and join on gemeindeschluessel. Example corrected query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Gemeinde, Radweg_zu_Gemeinde WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Radweg_zu_Gemeinde.gemeindeschluessel AND Gemeinde.plz > 96400;

issues.description: Concept: the relation linking Radwege to Gemeinden. Problem statement (Aufgabe 08) refers to Radwege / the Radweg_zu_Gemeinde relationship. In the solution file aufgabe08.sql the identifiers are inconsistent: the FROM clause uses Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde while the WHERE clause references Radweg_zu_Gemeinde. This mixes two different table names for the same conceptual relation and will produce a SQL error or incorrect result, preventing students from mapping the task requirement (count Radwege adjacent to Gemeinden with PLZ > 96400) to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix:
Use a single consistent table name for the Radweg-to-Gemeinde relationship. Replace Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde with Radweg_zu_Gemeinde in the FROM clause so both FROM and WHERE reference Radweg_zu_Gemeinde. For example:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM Gemeinde, Radweg_zu_Gemeinde
WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Radweg_zu_Gemeinde.gemeindeschluessel
  AND Gemeinde.plz > 96400
